claims.statement: The repository carries two independent CI definitions for the same monorepo: four GitHub Actions workflows under .github/workflows (deploy, e2e, wahapedia-sync, openwiki-update) and a two-stage GitLab pipeline in .gitlab-ci.yml (test, then build-images). Because production compose pulls the GHCR forceorg-* images, GitHub Actions is the pipeline that publishes what production runs, while the GitLab pipeline pushes to $CI_REGISTRY under different image names and only runs against a GitLab-hosted copy.

deploy.yml's single validate-and-build job runs the same validation prefix on every push and pull request to main: setup-node 20 with npm cache, npm ci, explicit `npx prisma generate --schema=packages/db-client/prisma/schema.prisma`, then `npm run lint` plus `npm run test:coverage --prefix packages/rules-engine-11e`, then `npm run build`. Any of these failing blocks the merge, and because the root scripts are `turbo run lint`/`turbo run build` the gate covers the whole workspace graph (lint is `tsc --noEmit` per package plus `next lint` for web).

All publishing steps in deploy.yml are guarded by `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`: only main pushes log in to ghcr.io as github.actor with GITHUB_TOKEN and push the api, web and sync-worker images; pull requests validate but publish nothing.

Because GHCR requires all-lowercase image names and this repository's name contains uppercase characters, deploy.yml first computes `ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY,,}` into the `imagename` step output; all three images (forceorg-api, forceorg-web, forceorg-sync-worker) are tagged with that lowercased prefix plus both `latest` and `github.sha`.

No CI workflow performs a deployment: publishing is the terminal step, and the published images are consumed by docker-compose.prod.yml, which pulls ghcr.io/fatpat81/beerhammer/forceorg-{api,web,sync-worker} with FORCEORG_TAG defaulting to `latest`. Because every main push also leaves an immutable commit-SHA tag, rollback is an operational act on the host — set FORCEORG_TAG to a previous commit SHA and pull again — not a pipeline.

e2e.yml runs on push and pull_request to main in a 20-minute job that does npm ci, prisma generate, `npm run build` with NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL set to http://localhost:4000/api (Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time, and apps/web/src/lib/api.ts reads it once as API_BASE), installs only Chromium, runs `npx playwright test --project="Desktop Chrome"` from apps/web, and always uploads apps/web/playwright-report/ for 14 days.

apps/web/playwright.config.ts declares two projects, Desktop Chrome and Mobile Safari (iPhone 14), but CI selects only Desktop Chrome and installs only Chromium, so WebKit/mobile coverage exists locally only. Under CI the config also sets forbidOnly (a committed test.only fails), retries 2, workers 1, and reporter html.

The Playwright webServer config starts only `npx next start -p 3456` with reuseExistingServer: false (so the suite can never adopt an unrelated server holding the port) and baseURL http://localhost:3456; the e2e job defines no services, database, or compose step, so calls to the API base URL fail during CI runs.

Because no API is running in the e2e job, the five specs in apps/web/e2e/critical-flows.spec.ts pass against the pages' hardcoded fallback datasets rather than real persistence: FALLBACK_CATALOG_DATASHEETS on /catalog, FALLBACK_CHANGELOG on /changelog, and the fallback army plus DEMO_FALLBACK_UNITS on the tabletop console. Specs requiring real writes would fail in CI, and removing fallback data from a page changes what the suite actually exercises.

wahapedia-sync.yml is triggered by cron `0 2 * * *` (daily 02:00 UTC) and workflow_dispatch, and is the production ETL runner rather than a merge gate: after npm ci and prisma generate it explicitly builds packages/types, packages/db-client and packages/rules-engine-11e, then runs `npm run worker:sync --prefix apps/sync-worker`, which executes tsx src/index.ts directly instead of a compiled dist.

The scheduled sync run receives only DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL and ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL from repo secrets; the two database URLs back the Prisma datasource's pooled url and directUrl, and ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is consumed by sendAlert(), which returns immediately when unset and is called only when updated > 0 || errors > 0 — so a clean no-delta run emits no notification.

A caught per-endpoint ETL failure is recorded as a SyncMetadata row with status ERROR and does not propagate, so the workflow stays green while only a thrown top-level error makes apps/sync-worker/src/index.ts exit 1; errors therefore surface through the webhook summary, not the workflow conclusion.

openwiki-update.yml (cron `0 8 * * *` plus manual dispatch, running on Node 22 while the application pipelines all pin Node 20) is what regenerates the generated pages under /openwiki: it clones with fetch-depth 0 so `openwiki code --update` can diff against the last documented commit, installs openwiki@0.7.0 with optional mermaid/jsdom for diagram validation, and runs `openwiki code --update --print` against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured by OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY, OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL and OPENWIKI_MODEL_ID. Generated pages should not be hand-edited; change source code or authored docs instead.

The OpenWiki step is continue-on-error, transient state openwiki/.run.json is deleted before committing, and the job opens or reuses a pull request from branch openwiki/update adding only openwiki, AGENTS.md, .github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml and CLAUDE.md when present; only afterwards does it exit 1 on failure, so a partially completed run still yields a reviewable PR holding the pages finished before the failure as the next run's baseline. Changes outside those paths are discarded by the run.

.gitlab-ci.yml sets default interruptible: true (a new push cancels the in-flight pipeline) and runs a node:20-alpine `test` job on merge_request_event or the default branch that installs git via apk, caches .npm/ and .turbo/ under ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}, and executes `npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline`, prisma generate, then `npx turbo run test build`.

GitLab's build-images stage runs on the default branch only, in docker:24.0.5 with a dind service, logging into $CI_REGISTRY and publishing $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE/web and $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE/api tagged latest and $CI_COMMIT_SHA. It never builds Dockerfile.sync-worker and does not use the GHCR forceorg-* names, so the sync-worker image exists only on GHCR — which is what production compose pulls.

The two pipelines gate on different commands: GitLab's MR check is `turbo run test build`, while GitHub's PR check is lint + rules-engine coverage + build and never invokes `turbo run test`. Since packages/rules-engine-11e is the only workspace with a `test` script the unit coverage overlaps today, but GitHub additionally enforces `turbo run lint`, which GitLab reaches only transitively through the build.

Every CI entrypoint regenerates the Prisma client explicitly even though the root postinstall script already runs `prisma generate --schema=packages/db-client/prisma/schema.prisma` during npm ci; the explicit steps are redundant but harmless, and at least one of the two must remain in any new workflow.

The committed CI contains no deploy, rollback, migration or release workflow, and no branch-protection/required-check configuration is stored in the repository, so which checks actually block a merge is enforced in hosted GitHub settings outside this tree.

Database schema migration is not a CI-stage concern in either pipeline: no workflow runs `prisma migrate deploy`. Migration happens at container start in the API image's entrypoint (apps/api/entrypoint.sh), which defaults DIRECT_URL to DATABASE_URL and applies pending Prisma migrations before exec'ing the server, and skips migrations entirely when DATABASE_URL is unset. A bad migration therefore surfaces as a container restart loop on the host, not as a failing pipeline.
